term_info: Full term commencing 1/1/2027; vote for 1; 6-year term. Judicial candidates run without party labels on the general ballot but are nominated in partisan primaries; parties below are the nominating party per the BOE list.

candidates.name: Daniel R. Hawkins
candidates.background: Elected to the Ohio Supreme Court in November 2024, took his seat in January 2025. Before that served on the Franklin County Court of Common Pleas (~11 years) and 13 years as a Franklin County prosecutor, including as head of the special victims unit.
promises: Stated judicial approach: 'Judges should just call balls and strikes... A judge's role [is] to say what is the law and not what they think the law should be'
Named U.S. Supreme Court Justices Scalia and Thomas as models
Said he wanted the court to 'maintain a good, conservative balance'
record: Wells Fargo Bank, N.A. v. Doberdruk, 2026-Ohio-2674: authored unanimous majority holding R.C. 2329.45 lets a borrower seek restitution if a foreclosure is later found improper
Doe v. Columbus, 2026-Ohio-1095: authored 5-2 majority holding preliminary injunctions blocking city ordinances are uniformly 'final orders' subject to immediate appeal

Joined Justice Pat DeWine's 4-3 majority in State v. King, 2026-Ohio-2656 (July 14, 2026), which overruled the Court's 1987 decision and held prosecutors may appeal a trial judge's post-verdict acquittal
candidates.correlation: Stated approach (plain-language textualism) is consistent in form with his opinions. His votes place him consistently in the Court's 4-3/5-2 conservative majorities. His Doberdruk majority ruling was unanimous and favored the borrower, showing his record is not uniformly aligned with one litigant class.

candidates.name: Marilyn Zayas
candidates.background: Judge on Ohio's First District Court of Appeals (Hamilton County) for about nine years; first elected in 2016 - the first person of Latino heritage elected to an Ohio appeals court. Born 1964 in East Harlem, NYC; B.S. in computer science; IT manager at Procter & Gamble (1988-1994); J.D., University of Cincinnati College of Law (1997). Ran for the Court in 2022 and lost to Justice Pat DeWine.
promises: Stated philosophy: 'to faithfully apply the law and constitution equally to everyone. There should not be any bias if someone has money or doesn't have money.'
Court 'must be a beacon of integrity, impartiality, and independence'
Accepted '$0 from corporate interests: energy, banking, and insurance companies'
Would expand Veterans, Mental Health, and Drug Courts
record: Authored a unanimous First District reversal of a juvenile court's permanent-custody termination order - UNVERIFIED as to the case name/citation
Sat by designation on the Ohio Supreme Court in multiple cases
2025 First District participation: concurred in In re J. Children (2025) and In re C/S Children (2025), affirming juvenile-court permanent-custody awards
Named 2024 Hispanic National Bar Association Latina Judge of the Year
candidates.correlation: Stated philosophy (law-applied-equally, independence from political influence, skepticism of overturning settled precedent) is consistent with her appellate record and public criticism of State v. King. Her $0-corporate-money pledge is a campaign posture with no judicial-record equivalent.

record: No specific notable rulings from her Common Pleas tenure or immigration-court service were verifiable in available public sources - UNVERIFIED beyond biographical facts

candidates.correlation: With no verifiable ruling record in the public domain, there is nothing to correlate against her campaign statements; voters can weigh only her experience claims and stated philosophy.
